newsitem.title: FRANCE: France must continue to produce combat jets-Chirac.
newsitem.headline: France must continue to produce combat jets-Chirac.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Saturday France must maintain its capacity to produce combat aircraft.

He was speaking at the inauguration of the 42nd Paris air show at Le Bourget where the number of up to date combat planes, and especially the countries who still have the capacity to produce them, has been steadily dropping for years.
"France, which is a great power, must maintain its capacity to produce combat aircraft," Chirac told reporters when visiting the exhibit area of the French Dassault Aviation firm.
Dassault hopes its Rafale fighter-bomber can challenge U.S. giants such as McDonnell Douglas which makes the F-15 and Lockheed Martin's F-16.

The Rafale, which has only so far been been sold to the French air force, also competes with the Eurofighter which is under development by Britain, Germany, Italy and Spain, and the Gripen light fighter from Sweden.

But industry executives say the huge costs of developing new military aircraft mean future planes will be built in cooperative ventures, such as the Eurofighter, on which British Aerospace Plc (BAe), Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa), Alenia of Italy and Casa of Spain are collaborating.

The previous conservative govermnent had planned to merge Dassault Aviation with the state-owned Aerospatiale group, as part of a defence industry consolidation announced by Chirac in February last year. A merger deal was expected at the airshow but with the arrival of a new Socialist government, the industry eagerly awaits news of the fate of the two groups.
